title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class) we produced one shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the same candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced structured workflow policies and could invoke ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We (1) condense provenance to a short methods paragraph pointing to archived execution and analysis artifacts, (2) provide a compact formal binary scoring rule used for the McNemar test with a concrete example drawn from archived scoring artifacts, and (3) add a nearest-work comparison that explicitly contrasts this study’s shared-generation paired design and bounded repair budget against close prior benchmarks and tool papers.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into network configuration commands, promising higher NetOps productivity. Yet syntax-correct commands can violate ordering, availability, or workflow constraints (for example, changing MTU without required shutdown or performing unsafe uplink switchover) and only reveal such semantic failures under closed-loop execution. Prior papers therefore advocate integrating verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers so that generated candidates are validated prior to enactment. However, many prior evaluations conflate generator variability with validator performance, making it difficult to isolate the marginal effect of an executable validator and a bounded repair policy. We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) whose objective was mechanistic: holding the generator fixed (a single shared initial candidate per task) measure whether an executable validator plus at-most-one repair iteration reduces semantic failures relative to an LLM-only suggestion workflow. The paired shared-candidate design removes generator-induced variance and directly measures validator/repair influence on identical candidates. We report full preregistration, execution accounting, a compact formalization of the binary scoring rule used for confirmatory testing, representative diagnostics, and a nearest-work comparison that situates our design choices among recent executable-benchmark and tool-augmentation studies.
sections.related_work: Two literature strands frame this study. First, executable emulation and closed-loop benchmarks (exemplified by recent NetOps benchmarks and emulation-grounded testbeds) emphasize that token- and syntax-level checks miss sequencing and stateful errors; closed-loop execution uncovers make-before-break mistakes, group-availability violations, and ordered-operation errors. Second, tool-augmented and bounded-autonomy architectures (generate→validate→repair, veto layers, translation-to-formal-model) are repeatedly proposed as practical safety measures for agentic NetOps. Prior benchmark and tool papers demonstrate that verification or emulation materially improves detection of semantic errors, but they typically evaluate generator and validator together and thus do not isolate validator marginal effects under identical generated outputs. Table 3 (nearest-work comparison) lists close verified references and marks where our paired shared-generation design and bounded repair budget differ from those prior works.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) prior to execution and specified a paired-binary confirmatory design with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks partitioned deterministically into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine; 40 tasks each). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified test was the exact two-sided McNemar. A bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified for the paired-difference estimate. The preregistration also fixed exclusion/contamination rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic reset controls, and sensitivity analyses.

Task generation and harness. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and carry structured payloads (initial_state, expected_final_state, natural-language intent, required_sequence, and difficulty metadata). The generator stage produced one shared initial candidate per task using the declared model gpt-5-mini (execution manifest: model_calls_used = 120; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 120). The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), an executable emulator/validator which enforces task-encoded workflow policies (fields including must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break) and returns a structured validator_trace. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair iteration when validator.violation_count > 0; repair prompts and traces would be archived when used.

Compact provenance paragraph (condensed). All primary execution and analysis artifacts required to reproduce reported accounting are archived and checksummed in the study bundle. Representative files include execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (task payloads and generator outputs), execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap parameters and seed). No technical exclusions or contamination flags occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv and analysis/contamination_summary.csv). See the archived execution and analysis bundle for full artifact manifests and checksums.

Formal binary scoring rule (compact). The confirmatory analysis used a deterministic mapping from scorer/validator JSON fields to a binary label Success ∈ {0,1} per episode. We define Success = 1 (pass) if and only if all of the following hold for the episode's scoring artifact:
1) scoring_status == "COMPLETED";
2) scorer_id == "deterministic_netops_validator_v5" (validator_version recorded as "5.0");
3) validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true AND validator_trace.violation_count == 0;
4) normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer (text-normalized canonical candidate equals the task reference); and
5) parsed_command_count >= required_command_count (validator parsed at least the required commands).
Otherwise Success = 0 (fail). This mapping was predetermined in the analysis plan and implemented by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.

Concrete example (artifact-grounded). execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json shows the following fields used above: "score": 1, "score_reason_code": "VALID_CONFIGURATION", "scorer_id": "deterministic_netops_validator_v5", "validator_version": "5.0", validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true, validator_trace.violation_count == 0, and normalized_response equals normalized_reference_answer. Under the formal rule this episode is labeled Success = 1 (pass). An exemplar failing artifact would have validator_trace.violation_count > 0 or validation_after.valid == false and would map to Success = 0; no such artifacts were produced in this run.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference point estimate = 0.00. The bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is degenerate: [0.00, 0.00]; this degeneracy follows from zero discordant pairs in the empirical table under the prespecified resampling scheme.

Per-topology counts (archived artifacts). The deterministic task partition produced 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology results (drawn from task manifest and scoring artifacts) are:
- Edge (40 pairs): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
- Core (40 pairs): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
- Leaf–spine (40 pairs): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
Representative scoring artifacts (for example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json) show normalized_response equals normalized_reference_answer, validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true, validator_trace.repair_applied == false, scorer_id == "deterministic_netops_validator_v5".

Repair activity and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count == 0 for all guarded episodes, repair_applied == false across the run and no repair_provider_trace artifacts exist. Secondary estimands (repair incidence, mean repair calls per successful task) are vacuous in this dataset; their vacuity is an empirical feature recorded in validator traces and in the execution manifest.

Contamination and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty and analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 with zero technical/instrumentation exclusions. deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms provider-call audits and pair accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cache_miss_count = 120; cross-condition cache reuse = false).
sections.discussion:
Statistical and substantive interpretation of the ceiling result. The paired shared-candidate design isolates validator/repair marginal effects by construction, but it also risks producing degenerate confirmatory outcomes when the generator routinely produces valid candidates for the selected task bank. That is the observed outcome: all shared initial candidates satisfied the emulator validator, so the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 and degenerate bootstrap CI reflect this ceiling and correctly indicate no observed difference between conditions under the prespecified design and task corpus.

Design trade-offs and concrete recommendations. The collected task_manifest difficulty metadata (fields such as dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, and difficulty level) and the observed absence of repairs suggest targeted preregistration changes to better exercise repair utility in future confirmatory runs: (1) independent generation per condition (allow separate generator draws per arm) to expose generator-induced errors; (2) prespecified prompt perturbation blocks to increase generator error incidence while retaining paired controls where informative; (3) focus confirmatory power on tasks with manifest-labeled 'very_hard' difficulty or high dependency_rule_count; (4) allow exploratory arms with expanded repair budgets (multiple repair iterations) to study repair convergence and cost. These suggestions follow directly from archived manifest fields and the recorded zero-repair outcome.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strong: deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audit logs, zero exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity is limited by task synthesis: validator checks were encoded against required_sequence fields in synthetic payloads and do not capture every vendor-specific or telemetry-limited failure present in diverse production networks. External validity is constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: preregistered power calculations assumed a nontrivial baseline failure rate (~0.40) and targeted absolute reduction 0.15; the observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions, rendering the confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow using a shared-generation paired design and a deterministic emulator validator. All 120 shared initial candidates passed the validator, producing n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00]). The result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and shows that a shared-generation paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects but can mask repair utility when the generator is well-calibrated for the selected tasks. We provide artifact-grounded diagnostics, a compact formal scoring rule and example, and concrete preregistered design recommendations for follow-up confirmatory work that aims to exercise repair behavior and quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
